scenario_title: Exploring Number Formations and Code Creation
scenario_summary: A journey through the mathematical concepts of permutations and combinations, using sets and simple mathematical operations.
visual_setting: Clean, dark background with LaTeX notation, geometric primitives, and text labels.

scenes.title: Forming 3-Digit Numbers
scenes.narration: How many 3-digit numbers can be formed from the digits 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5?
scenes.animation_description: A set of 5 nodes labeled 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5. Arrows show the selection of 3 nodes for the first, second, and third positions.
scenes.manim_hint: Use `Dot` for nodes and `Arrow` for connections.

scenes.title: Repetition Allowed
scenes.narration: If repetition is allowed, how many numbers can be formed?
scenes.animation_description: Arrows now loop back to the set of 5 nodes, allowing the same node to be selected multiple times.

scenes.title: Repetition Not Allowed
scenes.narration: If repetition is not allowed, how many numbers can be formed?
scenes.animation_description: Arrows move to the next node in the set, ensuring no node is selected more than once.

scenes.title: Even 3-Digit Numbers
scenes.narration: How many 3-digit even numbers can be formed from the digits 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6?
scenes.animation_description: A set of 6 nodes labeled 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6. Arrows show the selection of 3 nodes, with a specific constraint for the last position.
scenes.manim_hint: Use `Dot` for nodes and `Arrow` for connections, with a condition for the last node.

scenes.title: 4-Letter Code
scenes.narration: How many 4-letter codes can be formed using the first 10 letters of the English alphabet?
scenes.animation_description: A set of 10 nodes labeled A to J. Arrows show the selection of 4 nodes without repetition.
scenes.manim_hint: Use `Dot` for nodes and `Arrow` for connections, with a loop to ensure no repetition.

scenes.title: 5-Digit Telephone Numbers
scenes.narration: How many 5-digit telephone numbers can be constructed using the digits 0 to 9 if each number starts with 67?
scenes.animation_description: A set of 10 nodes labeled 0 to 9. Arrows show the selection of 3 nodes after the first two fixed digits 6 and 7.
scenes.manim_hint: Use `Dot` for nodes and `Arrow` for connections, with a loop to ensure no repetition.

scenes.title: Coin Toss Outcomes
scenes.narration: A coin is tossed 3 times. How many possible outcomes are there?
scenes.animation_description: A set of 2 nodes labeled H (Heads) and T (Tails). Arrows show the selection of 3 nodes for the three tosses.
scenes.manim_hint: Use `Dot` for nodes and `Arrow` for connections.

scenes.title: Signal Generation
scenes.narration: Given 5 flags of different colours, how many different signals can be generated if each signal requires the use of 2 flags, one below the other?
scenes.animation_description: A set of 5 nodes labeled A to E. Arrows show the selection of 2 nodes for the two positions.
scenes.manim_hint: Use `Dot` for nodes and `Arrow` for connections.

scenes.title: Revealing Formulas
scenes.narration: Let's reveal the formulas for these calculations.
scenes.animation_description: Formulas for permutations and combinations fade in: $P(n, r) = n! / (n-r)!$ and $C(n, r) = n! / (r!(n-r)!)$.

scenes.title: Recap
scenes.narration: In summary, we learned how to calculate permutations and combinations using sets and simple mathematical operations.
scenes.animation_description: A recap of the formulas and examples used throughout the video.
scenes.manim_hint: Use `MathTex` for the formulas and `Text` for the recap text.
